topic_summary: Analysis of Vatican II (1962-1965) as a composite doctrinal shift rather than a single coherent reinterpretation. The Council produced 16 documents enacting modernizing changes (liturgical reform, religious freedom, ecumenism) while claiming continuity with tradition. The research context frames this as a 'non-break composite test'—examining whether Vatican II represents one contested kernel with multiple readings or an overdetermined convergence of distinct structural tensions.

key_entities: Pope Paul VI (successor; guided Council to conclusion)
Progressive theologians (de Lubac, Congar, Bea; suppressed under Pius XII, ascendant at Council)
Conservative opposition (Ottaviani, Siri, Ruffini; Coetus Internationalis Patrum)
Council Fathers (2,000+ bishops voting on documents)
Post-conciliar implementation bodies (liturgical commissions, national conferences)
key_tensions: Aggiornamento (updating) vs doctrinal continuity (John XXIII's dual mandate)
Progressive reform vs conservative preservation (factional voting blocs)
Conciliar intent vs post-conciliar implementation (Latin preservation mandate vs actual elimination)
Hermeneutic of continuity vs hermeneutic of rupture (Benedict XVI vs progressive/traditionalist wings)
Compromise-induced textual ambiguity vs interpretive clarity (10-12% rejection rates on key documents)
key_mechanisms: Voting threshold requirements (producing compromise documents to achieve supermajorities)
Periti influence (expert theologians drafting and revising texts)
Post-conciliar implementation commissions (translating documents into practice, often exceeding textual mandates)
key_absences: No new dogmas defined; no heresies condemned (departure from prior ecumenical council pattern)
Minimal discussion of enforcement mechanisms for continuity claims (how to prevent interpretive drift)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Continuity reading holds that magisterial teaching cannot reverse itself on matters of faith and morals; progressive rupture reading holds that Dignitatis Humanae reversed prior teaching on religious freedom. No single framework can hold both 'the Church cannot reverse teaching X' and 'the Church did reverse teaching X' as simultaneously true.

Continuity reading holds that Vatican II documents are authoritative magisterial teaching requiring assent; traditionalist rupture reading holds that Vatican II documents contain errors and may be resisted. No single framework can hold both 'these documents bind conscience' and 'these documents may be rejected' as simultaneously true.

Progressive rupture reading holds that the break with tradition is legitimate and Spirit-guided; traditionalist rupture reading holds that the break with tradition is illegitimate and heterodox. Both agree on rupture but assign opposite normative valence. A single framework cannot hold both 'this rupture is divinely authorized' and 'this rupture is heterodox' as simultaneously true.

omegas.description: Does the kernel/reading framework collapse under composite overdetermination? If Vatican II is genuinely multiple independent shifts (liturgical, ecumenical, political) rather than one contested interpretation, then continuity/rupture debate is a category error—different components exhibit different degrees of change. The 10-12% rejection rates varying by document suggest independent ε values per component. Composite_overdetermination_reading deferred but may be the structurally correct frame.
omegas.source: Deferred axis composite_overdetermination_reading + research context 'non-break composite test'

omegas.description: Who has authority to interpret ambiguous conciliar texts? Post-conciliar implementation (Latin elimination despite §36 mandate) suggests implementation bodies exceeded textual authority. Is this a Rope (coordination problem) or Snare (intentional ambiguity enabling capture)? Progressive reading treats it as legitimate development; traditionalist as heterodox drift. No mechanism in conciliar documents to adjudicate.
omegas.source: Tension between conciliar intent and post-conciliar implementation + absence of enforcement mechanisms

omegas.description: Vatican II defined no new dogmas and condemned no heresies—departure from prior ecumenical council pattern. Does this lower the binding force of conciliar teaching, enabling competing interpretations? Continuity reading says no (pastoral councils still authoritative); rupture readings (both progressive and traditionalist) implicitly say yes (treating documents as revisable). Absence of dogmatic definitions may be structural cause of interpretive instability.
omegas.source: Absence inventory: no new dogmas defined

omegas.description: Supermajority requirements produced compromise documents satisfying neither faction. 10-12% rejection rates on religious freedom, ecumenism, and modern world suggest structural minorities. Did voting thresholds create ambiguities as Snares (enabling post-conciliar capture) or as Ropes (necessary coordination cost)? Traditionalist reading treats as Snare; continuity reading as Rope. Mechanism itself may determine interpretive instability.

Continuity reading grounds authority in ressourcement (return to patristic sources). But if patristic sources authorize novelty (e.g., religious freedom via Lactantius), is this continuity or rupture? The mechanism (return to sources) may generate the very discontinuity it claims to avoid. Paradox unresolved in continuity reading's constraint structure.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan): papal magisterium benefits from continuity claim, but ressourcement mechanism may undermine it
